translations.answer: Static IK only indicates that a certain posture may have a joint solution, but does not necessarily satisfy task conditions and dynamic reachability. This post constructs a dynamic reachability map by sampling 20 million trajectories and postures per arm, and verifies it with an IK solver; however, there is no real-world result, so it is only a candidate method.
translations.applicability: Suitable for selecting operational targets in two-arm or full-body manipulation.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is lacking.
translations.details.attempts.0: Construct a dynamic reachability graph based on task conditions.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Verify the sampled reachability graph using an IK solver.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Filter candidate targets before planning using the reachability graph, as the post suggests.
translations.details.environments.0: Humanoid two-arm operation framework; 20 million trajectories and postures per arm sampled.
translations.details.limits.0: Lack of sampling range, IK error, dynamic constraints, and hardware results.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Completed open-source implementation, but no real-world success rate.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: The operational target may be kinematically reachable but dynamically unexecutable.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Reachability graph cannot replace collision, torque, velocity, and self-collision checks.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Only considering static IK does not cover task conditions and dynamic reachability.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The post does not provide failure case examples.
translations.media_summaries.0: The screenshot video frame includes scene point clouds and humanoid models, showing a colored reachable region; no legend, error threshold, or collision information is present.
